summary: ITU-T G.709 introduced new ODU containers (ODU0, ODU4, ODU2e, and ODUflex) and more flexibility. This document updates the ODU-related parts of RFC 4328 with GMPLS signaling extensions to control the full set of OTN features.

eli5.summary: Optical networks have new sizes of shipping containers. This teaches the signaling system how to ask for each size when setting up a path.

subtitle: How GMPLS signaling asks for the new ODU0, ODU2e, ODU4 and ODUflex containers in optical transport networks.

tldr.problem: ITU-T G.709 added new containers (ODU0, ODU2e, ODU4, ODUflex) and a 1.25 Gbps tributary slot size, but the GMPLS signaling in RFC 4328 only covered the 2001 revision of G.709 and the deprecated auto-MSI mode.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC extends the RSVP-TE traffic parameters with new Signal Types and a Bit_Rate field, defines a new OTN-TDM Generalized Label that carries a Tributary Port Number and a bit map of tributary slots, and adds procedures for label errors and hitless ODUflex resizing.
tldr.outcome: It updates the ODU-related parts of RFC 4328 so a GMPLS control plane can set up paths over the full set of G.709 containers. It has since been updated by RFC 7892.

today: RFC 7139 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2014. It updates RFC 4328 and has itself been updated by RFC 7892.

sections.title: Why G.709 Signaling Needed an Update
sections.content:
An Optical Transport Network (OTN) carries client signals inside containers called Optical channel Data Units (ODUs). The 2012 revision of ITU-T G.709 added new containers (ODU0, ODU2e, ODU4 and ODUflex) and a new tributary slot (TS) granularity of 1.25 Gbps. The older 2.5 Gbps granularity stays in use on legacy interfaces, so ODU1, ODU2 and ODU3 now come in two flavours.

RFC 4328 described GMPLS signaling for the 2001 revision of G.709. It cannot signal the new Signal Types or the new mapping and multiplexing options, and it supports only the deprecated auto-MSI mode, where the Tributary Port Number (TPN) is assigned automatically on transmit and not checked on receive.

This document updates the ODU-related parts of RFC 4328 with RSVP-TE extensions. It follows the framework in RFC 7062 and the evaluation in RFC 7096, and it relies on the new OTN-TDM Switching Type defined in RFC 7138.
sections.eli5: Shipping containers came in a few sizes, and now there are new sizes and new ways to pack them. The old booking form had no boxes for those, so this RFC adds them.

sections.title: Signal Types and Traffic Parameters
sections.content:
The traffic parameters travel in the OTN-TDM SENDER_TSPEC object (Class 12, C-Type 7) in the Path message and the OTN-TDM FLOWSPEC object (Class 9, C-Type 7) in the Resv message. They hold a Signal Type, NVC (number of virtual components), a multiplier MT and a Bit_Rate.

The RFC adds Signal Type values to those in RFC 4328: 4 for ODU4, 9 for OCh at 100 Gbps, 10 for ODU0, 11 for ODU2e, and 20, 21 and 22 for the ODUflex variants. For ODUflex, NVC MUST be 0 and MT MUST be 1.

For ODUflex, Bit_Rate is the nominal bit rate in bytes per second, encoded as a 32-bit IEEE single-precision floating-point number. For other Signal Types it MUST be zero on transmission and ignored on receipt. For ODUflex(GFP), the value MUST be one of 80 values: 1 to 8 times the ODU2.ts rate, 9 to 32 times the ODU3.ts rate, or 33 to 80 times the ODU4.ts rate, so the number of tributary slots can be deduced from it.

Nodes check the request. If a node cannot support the Signal Type, NVC and Bit_Rate it sends a PathErr with "Traffic Control Error/Service unsupported". A zero MT, or a nonzero NVC on a Signal Type other than ODU1, ODU2 or ODU3, produces a PathErr with "Bad Tspec value".
sections.eli5: The booking form says what size of container you want and, for the stretchy kind, exactly how much room it needs. Any stop on the route that cannot handle it sends the form back with a note.

sections.title: Counting Tributary Slots for ODUflex
sections.content:
An ODUflex(CBR) signal needs a whole number of tributary slots in the higher-order ODUk link, and the count depends on that link. The RFC gives N as the ceiling of the ODUflex(CBR) nominal bit rate times (1 + its tolerance), divided by the ODTUk.ts nominal bit rate times (1 - the higher-order OPUk tolerance). The ODUflex(CBR) tolerance is fixed at 100 ppm and the higher-order tolerance is 20 ppm, so the tolerance does not need to be signaled.

The worked example asks for 2.5 Gbps from node A to node C. On the HO ODU4 link from A to B, N1 = 2 tributary slots are reserved. On the HO ODU2 link from B to C, N2 = 3. The same service can therefore use a different number of slots on different links.
sections.eli5: A big suitcase may take two shelves in one warehouse but three smaller shelves in another. Each stop works out how many shelves it needs from the suitcase's size.

sections.title: The OTN-TDM Generalized Label
sections.content:
The GENERALIZED_LABEL object MUST use a new format with the OTN-TDM Switching Type. It says how a lower-order ODUj is multiplexed into a higher-order ODUk. It has a 12-bit TPN, a reserved byte, a 12-bit Length, a variable Bit Map and padding bits that bring the label to a multiple of four bytes.

The TPN lets the far end of the link demultiplex correctly. It is written into the MSI byte(s) of the OPUk overhead at the ingress end of the link. Only the lower 6 bits are significant for an HO ODU1, ODU2 or ODU3 and the lower 7 bits for an HO ODU4. The remaining bits MUST be 0, and for ODUj mapped directly into OTUk the TPN is 0. The RFC's tables give assignment rules: some are fixed (equal to the slot number) and some flexible (any value not used by other lower-order ODUs on the link).

Length is the number of bits in the Bit Map, which is the total number of tributary slots in the link. The values 4 and 16 indicate 2.5 Gbps granularity, and 2, 8, 32 and 80 indicate 1.25 Gbps granularity. When an ODUk is mapped straight into OTUk, Length MUST be 0 and no bit map is included. Each bit in the map marks one slot as used (1) or not (0).

One example: a label with TPN = 2, Length = 8 and bit map 01000000 places an ODU0 in the second slot of an ODU2 that has 8 slots.
sections.eli5: The label is a seating chart: a row of checkboxes shows which seats in the big container are taken, plus a ticket number so the other end knows which passenger sits there.

sections.title: Label Procedures and Errors
sections.content:
The ingress node MUST send a Path message that names the OTN-TDM Switching Type and the right G-PID in the GENERALIZED_LABEL_REQUEST. It MAY add a Label ERO subobject, a LABEL_SET or a SUGGESTED_LABEL, and for bidirectional LSPs it MUST generate an UPSTREAM_LABEL.

A downstream or egress node builds the label from the requested Signal Type and its free tributary slots: it sets the bits for the reserved slots and assigns a valid TPN that does not collide with the TPNs of existing lower-order connections on that link. It also configures its Expected MSI (ExMSI) from that TPN. The upstream node reads the label, finds the reserved slots, and writes the TPN into the MSI overhead so the downstream node can detect a mismatch.

A label is unacceptable if it breaks local policy, has an invalid Length, claims 1.25 Gbps granularity on a link that supports only 2.5 Gbps, breaks the TPN rules, or has a count of 1 bits that disagrees with the traffic parameters. The node then MUST send a ResvErr (or PathErr for an upstream label) with "Routing problem/Unacceptable label value".

Virtual concatenation of ODU1, ODU2 and ODU3 follows RFC 6344 and is not changed. The RFC notes that G.709 does not support it for other Signal Types.
sections.eli5: The next stop picks free seats, writes its choice on the seating chart and sends it back. If the chart makes no sense, the stop sends it back with a note saying so.

sections.title: Hitless Resizing of ODUflex(GFP)
sections.content:
G.709's companion standard G.7044 describes hitless resizing of ODUflex(GFP) with the LCR and BWR protocols in the data plane. In the control plane, signaling is REQUIRED to start the adjustment, and the Shared Explicit (SE) reservation style from RFC 3209 is used.

A resizable connection (Signal Type 21) MUST be created with the SE style, otherwise a "Conflicting reservation style" error MUST be generated when resizing. To grow, the ingress sends a new Path message with the same Tunnel ID and a new LSP ID. Downstream nodes compare old and new traffic parameters, reserve the extra slots and answer with a Resv carrying both old and new labels. The ingress then SHOULD send a PathTear to delete the old state.

To shrink, the ingress SHOULD also send an SE Path message, and afterwards SHOULD send a ResvErr to tear down the old control state.
sections.eli5: If a stretchy container needs more room, you book the bigger size alongside the old one, switch over, and then cancel the old booking, so nothing is interrupted.

sections.title: Backward Compatibility with RFC 4328
sections.content:
Networks already run RFC 4328 for nodes that support the 2001 G.709 revision. Nodes supporting this document SHOULD support RFC 7138 and MAY support RFC 4328 signaling. A node that supports both is not required to translate an LSP between the two procedures. An ingress that supports both MAY choose using routing information or local policy.

A node that does not support this document answers with a PathErr that has a "Routing problem/Switching Type" indication.

The RFC also changes G-PID values: 47 is renamed from "G.709 ODUj" to "ODU-2.5G", 56 from "ESCON" to "SBCON/ESCON", and new G-PIDs 66 (ODU-1.25G) and 67 (ODU-any) cover multiplexing by granularity.
sections.eli5: Old and new equipment can live in the same network. A stop that does not know the new forms replies that it does not understand them.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The RFC only changes the information carried by the existing signaling, so it states that it introduces no new security considerations for GMPLS signaling. It points to RFC 3473 and RFC 4328 for security measures, and to RFC 5920 for an overview of GMPLS control-plane threats.

IANA assigned C-Type 7 (OTN-TDM) for both FLOWSPEC and SENDER_TSPEC, added and updated G-PID values, and created an "OTN Signal Type" subregistry. New values there are assigned through Standards Action.
sections.eli5: Only the contents of the forms changed, not who can send them, so the security rules stay as they were.

fields.name: Signal Type
fields.desc: Which ODU or OCh signal is requested.

fields.name: NVC
fields.desc: Number of virtual components; MUST be 0 for ODUflex.

fields.name: Bit_Rate
fields.desc: ODUflex nominal rate in bytes per second as an IEEE single-precision float; zero for other types.

fields.desc: Number of bits in the Bit Map, which is the number of tributary slots; 0 when ODUk maps into OTUk.
